mainTopic: Finding which תולדה רב פפא meant is unlike its אב (צרורות of רגל), and the רב and שמואל dispute over the meaning of מבעה
overview: רב פפא taught that some of the main damage categories (אבות) have sub-types (תולדות) that are not like them. The גמרא searches for which category he meant. Obstacles in the street turn out to be just like בור or שור. The תולדות of מבעה and of אש also turn out to be just like their אב, so neither can be his example. The answer is רגל: צרורות, pebbles kicked up by a walking animal, pay only חצי נזק by a tradition, yet they still count as a תולדה of רגל. For רב פפא this is because they are paid from the best property. For רבא, who was unsure about that, it is because they are exempt in רשות הרבים. The גמרא then asks what the משנה's word מבעה means. רב says אדם and שמואל says שן, and each brings a פסוק and a grammar argument. In the end, רב reasons that שור already covers all ox damage, while רב יהודה explains that for שמואל, שור means the horn and מבעה means the tooth, which enjoys the damage it does.

steps.title: Obstacles not declared ownerless are still just like their main category
steps.stepSummary: Even if the owner did not make the obstacles הפקר, they are fully בור for שמואל and fully שור for רב, so they cannot be רב פפא's example.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did not declare them ownerless: according to שמואל, who says we learn all of them from his pit, they are just Pit. And according to רב, who says we learn all of them from his ox, they are just Ox!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the other side of the case: obstacles the owner did NOT declare ownerless. It shows that this case also fails as an example for רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous lines already dealt with obstacles that were made הפקר. Now, for the case where they were not, each opinion puts them fully inside one main category. For שמואל they are בור, and for רב they are שור. Either way they are a normal תולדה that acts like its אב, which is not the kind of example רב פפא was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned all of them from his pit (שמואל's view)
we learned all of them from his ox (רב's view)

phrases.english: And if he did not declare them ownerless –
phrases.notes: "Them" means the stone, knife or load a person left in the public street, from the lines just before this.

phrases.english: if according to Shmuel, who says:
we learned all of them from his pit,
this is the same as Pit;
and if according to Rav, who says:
we learned all of them from his ox,
this is the same as Ox!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes rejecting the obstacles case by covering the case where they were not declared ownerless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב פפא's 'תולדות not like their אב' refers to obstacles in the public domain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For obstacles not declared ownerless, שמואל puts them fully inside בור and רב puts them fully inside שור, and either way they behave exactly like that אב.

steps.title: Why obstacles really match the features of a pit
steps.stepSummary: The features that make בור unique (made in a way that can damage, your property, your job to guard) all apply to obstacles too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about Pit? Its making is set up to cause damage, it is your property, and guarding it is your job. These obstacles too: they are set up to cause damage, they are your property, and guarding them is your job!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the defining features of בור and shows that obstacles share every one of them. This backs up the claim that they are just like בור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove a תולדה acts like its אב, you check whether it shares the אב's key features. בור has three: it is made in a way that can damage, it belongs to you, and you must guard it. Obstacles in the street have all three, so there is no reason to treat them differently from בור.

keyTerms.meaning: from the start it is made in a way that damages

phrases.english: What is special about Pit –
that its initial making is for damage,
and it is your property, and its guarding is upon you;
these too – their initial making is for damage,
and they are your property, and their guarding is upon you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1's claim (for שמואל) that obstacles are exactly like בור.
steps.raayaObject: That a תולדה of בור is treated exactly like בור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A feature-by-feature comparison: obstacles share all of בור's defining traits.

steps.title: New suggestion: רב פפא meant the sub-types of מבעה
steps.stepSummary: Since תולדה of בור is like בור, the גמרא says רב פפא must have been referring to the תולדות of מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a sub-type of Pit is like Pit, and when רב פפא spoke, he was talking about a sub-type of מבעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that בור's sub-types act like בור, and offers a new idea: רב פפא was talking about מבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קרן, שן, רגל and now בור all ruled out, the גמרא moves to another main category from the משנה, מבעה. This is a new proposal, and the next steps will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the four main damagers in the משנה; its meaning is debated

phrases.english: Rather, a sub-type of Pit is like Pit,
and when Rav Pappa said it –
phrases.notes: He means רב פפא's line that some תולדות are not like their אב.

phrases.english: it was about a sub-type of Maveh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the בור discussion and proposes a new target for רב פפא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the subject of רב פפא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רב פפא was talking about obstacles, which are sub-types of בור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Obstacles are just like בור, so רב פפא must mean the sub-types of מבעה.

steps.title: What is מבעה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what מבעה actually is, to test the new suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the category מבעה means. This sets up the next two steps, which check each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether מבעה can have sub-types that differ from it depends on what מבעה is. There is a famous disagreement on this between רב and שמואל, so the גמרא will check both views.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of מבעה so the step 3 suggestion can be tested.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the category מבעה refers to, and so what its sub-types would be.

steps.title: For שמואל, מבעה is שן, which is already settled
steps.stepSummary: If מבעה means שן, we already established that תולדה of שן is like שן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If according to שמואל, who says מבעה is Eating: we already established that a sub-type of Eating is like Eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea using שמואל's view and shows that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says מבעה means שן, damage done by an animal's eating. Earlier the גמרא already showed that שן's sub-types act like שן. So under שמואל, מבעה cannot be the category with differing sub-types.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth: damage by an animal eating

phrases.english: If according to Shmuel, who says:
Maveh is Tooth –
but we already established that a sub-type of Tooth is like Tooth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: מַבְעֶה זוֹ שֵׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the step 3 suggestion using שמואל's definition of מבעה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב פפא meant the תולדות of מבעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under שמואל, מבעה is שן, and שן's sub-types were already shown to be just like it.

steps.title: For רב, מבעה is אדם, but what sub-types would a person have?
steps.stepSummary: If מבעה means a person causing damage, it is unclear how there could be any אב and תולדה split at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If according to רב, who says מבעה is Man: what main types and what sub-types does it have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea using רב's view and asks what sub-types a person could even have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says מבעה means אדם, a person who damages with his own body. A person is liable for whatever damage he does, so there seems to be no natural way to split this into a main type and sub-types.

keyTerms.meaning: Man: damage a person causes himself
sub-types that come from a main category

phrases.english: If according to Rav, who says:
Maveh is Man –

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אָבוֹת וּמַאי תּוֹלָדוֹת אִית בֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: what main types and what sub-types are there in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְרַב, דְּאָמַר: מַבְעֶה זֶה אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the step 3 suggestion using רב's definition of מבעה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב פפא meant the תולדות of מבעה, under רב's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Damage by a person seems to be one uniform category, so there is no clear אב and תולדה to compare.

steps.title: Proposal: awake is the main type, asleep is the sub-type
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אב of אדם is damaging while awake, and תולדה is damaging while asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the main type is when awake, and the sub-type is when asleep;
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the question about אדם. This is only a suggestion, and the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a person damaging while awake is the standard case, and damaging while asleep is a weaker sub-type that might be treated differently. If so, this would be a תולדה that is not like its אב, just as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introducing a suggestion)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
the main type – awake, the sub-type – asleep;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 6's question about אדם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no possible sub-type of אדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe a sleeping person is a sub-type that is treated differently from an awake person.

steps.title: A משנה says a person is liable whether awake or asleep
steps.stepSummary: The awake and asleep split fails, because a משנה says a person is always fully liable, awake or asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: a person is always forewarned, whether awake or asleep!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the awake and asleep proposal by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a person is always fully liable, whether he is awake or asleep. So a sleeping person is treated the same as an awake one. Even if 'asleep' were a sub-type, it would be just like its אב, so it cannot be רב פפא's example.
steps.whatToRemember: So far: obstacles fall under בור or שור, מבעה as שן was already settled, and מבעה as אדם has no awake and asleep split, since a person is liable either way. The next step tries a new example, and step 20 gives the final answer.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: a person is always forewarned,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the מסכתא (26a). "Forewarned" here means he always pays in full.

phrases.english: whether awake or asleep!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 7 proposal using a משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposal that a sleeping person is a תולדה that differs from its אב (an awake person).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה makes awake and asleep the same in law, so there is no difference between them.

steps.title: A new suggestion: spit and phlegm
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the תולדה of a person (מבעה) that is different from its אב is damage done by his phlegm or spit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps רב פפא meant a person's phlegm and spit.
steps.whatsHappening: Awake versus asleep did not work, so the גמרא offers a new example of a תולדה of אדם: damage caused by a person's phlegm or spit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is still to find an אדם-type תולדה whose law is different from the אב. Spit and phlegm come from a person but are not his body, so maybe they follow different rules.

phrases.english: Rather, his phlegm and his spit.
phrases.notes: He means: maybe this is what רב פפא was talking about as a different kind of תולדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected awake/asleep split with a new candidate
steps.terutzMaskana: Spit and phlegm could be the different תולדה of אדם

steps.title: Asking how the spit case works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the exact case of spit damage would be.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact situation, setting up a two-sided test of the suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spit can do damage while it is flying through the air or after it lands. The גמרא is about to check both options.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details of the new suggestion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When exactly does the spit cause the damage

steps.title: Spit is either a person's own force or a pit
steps.stepSummary: If spit damages while flying, it is the person's own force; if after landing, everyone agrees it is בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it damages while moving, that is his own force. If it damages after it comes to rest, then according to both רב and שמואל it is a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both versions of the spit case fit into categories we already know, so it is not a special תולדה of אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While flying, the spit is like a stone the person threw, so it is just אדם itself (כחו). After landing, it is an obstacle lying in a public place, which is בור. Either way it is not a new אדם-type תולדה with its own rules.

keyTerms.meaning: his force; damage done by something a person sent out
after it has come to rest
pit; an obstacle that damages while staying in place

steps.confusionAlert: Damage done by something a person throws or sends flying counts as the person himself doing it. It is not a separate category.

phrases.english: If they damage while they are moving,
it is his own force!
If after it comes to rest,
both according to רב and according to שמואל,
phrases.notes: רב and שמואל argue only about obstacles that were not made ownerless. Spit is ownerless, so even רב agrees it counts as a pit.

phrases.english: this is a pit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both versions of the case asked about in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects spit and phlegm as the different תולדה of אדם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each version of the case is already either אדם itself or בור

steps.title: The תולדה of מבעה is like מבעה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תולדה of מבעה follows the same rules as מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תולדה of מבעה is like מבעה.
steps.whatsHappening: Every attempt failed, so the גמרא concludes that מבעה is not what רב פפא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ends the מבעה branch. Its תולדות work just like the אב.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the four main damagers; here being tested as אָדָם
a sub-category coming from a main category

steps.whatToRemember: So far קרן, שן, רגל, בור and מבעה all have תולדות that work just like their אב. The search for רב פפא's case continues with אש in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, the תולדה of מבעה is like מבעה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the last suggestion failed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מבעה's תולדות have the same law as מבעה

steps.title: Perhaps רב פפא meant a תולדה of fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב פפא was talking about a תולדה of אש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רב פפא said it, he meant a תולדה of fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new candidate: maybe the different תולדה is one of אש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מבעה failed, the next category to check is אש. The following steps test this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: fire; one of the four main damagers

phrases.english: And when רב פפא said it,
phrases.notes: This refers back to his statement that some תולדות are not like their אב.

phrases.english: it was about a תולדה of fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קָאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אַתּוֹלָדָה דְאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing מבעה, offers a new reading of רב פפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which category רב פפא meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא was talking about מבעה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא was talking about אש

steps.title: What is a תולדה of fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a תולדה of אש is and suggests items on a roof blown down by a normal wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a תולדה of fire? Suppose it is his stone, knife, or load that he left on top of his roof, and they fell in a normal wind and caused damage.
steps.whatsHappening: To test the fire idea, the גמרא first needs an example of a תולדה of אש, so it suggests things on a roof blown down by the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are like fire because the wind moves them and makes them cause damage. The word 'אילימא' tells us this example is about to be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say; introduces a suggestion that will be tested

phrases.english: What is a תולדה of fire?
If you say his stone, his knife, or his load
that he left on top of his roof,
and they fell in a normal wind and caused damage;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case needed to test the אש suggestion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of a תולדה of אש

steps.title: Items damaging while falling are just fire
steps.stepSummary: If the items damage while the wind carries them, this is simply אש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they damage while they are moving, this is fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the example: items damaging while the wind carries them are acting exactly like fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire damages when the wind carries it. Items pushed by the wind that damage while moving are doing the same thing, so there is no difference between them and the אב.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If they damage while they are moving,
this is fire,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי בַּהֲדֵי דְּאָזְלוּ קָא מַזְּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the example offered in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The roof-items example as a different תולדה of אש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Damaging while carried by the wind is exactly how אש works, so the law is the same

steps.title: Proving the roof items match fire exactly
steps.stepSummary: The features that define אש (another force mixed in, your property, your duty to guard it) are all present in the roof items.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes fire special? Another force is mixed in with it, and it is your property and guarding it is your job. These too have another force mixed in, and they are your property and guarding them is your job!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by listing what makes fire its own category and showing the roof items have every one of those features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire is special because wind helps it spread, it belongs to you, and you must watch it. The roof items have all three: the wind moves them, they are yours, and you must watch them. So they are fully like fire and are no different.

keyTerms.meaning: another force is mixed in (like the wind)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the basic definition of אש: your property, moved by another force, which you must guard.

phrases.english: What is different about fire?
That another force is mixed in with it,
phrases.notes: The other force is the wind that carries the fire.

phrases.english: and it is your property and guarding it is your job;

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי נָמֵי – כֹּחַ אַחֵר מְעוֹרָב בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: these too have another force mixed in with them,
and they are your property and guarding them is your job!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 15 by comparing what defines each
steps.raayaObject: That the roof items have the same law as אש
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing the defining features of fire with those of the roof items

steps.title: The תולדה of fire is like fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תולדה of אש follows the same rules as אש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תולדה of fire is like fire.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the roof items match fire completely, the גמרא concludes that אש is not what רב פפא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the אש branch. Its תולדות have the same law as the אב.

keyTerms.meaning: like fire; the same law as fire

phrases.english: Rather, the תולדה of fire is like fire,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from steps 15 and 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אש's תולדות have the same law as אש

steps.title: Perhaps רב פפא meant a תולדה of foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב פפא was talking about a תולדה of רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רב פפא said it, he meant a תולדה of foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more candidate: a תולדה of רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After בור, מבעה and אש have all failed, this is the next try at explaining רב פפא. It seems strange, since רגל was already discussed, and the next step points that out.

keyTerms.meaning: foot; damage an animal does by walking

phrases.english: And when רב פפא said it,
it was about a תולדה of foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קָאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא – אַתּוֹלָדָה דְרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing אש, offers a new reading of רב פפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which category רב פפא meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא was talking about אש
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא was talking about רגל

steps.title: But we already said foot's תולדה is like foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it already showed the תולדה of רגל is like רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Foot?! But we already established that the תולדה of foot is like foot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects: we already settled earlier that רגל's תולדות work like רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, the גמרא showed that an animal damaging with its body or hair while walking has the same law as רגל. So how can רב פפא mean רגל?

phrases.english: Foot?!
But we already established that the תולדה of foot is like foot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רגל suggestion of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב פפא meant רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the earlier conclusion that רגל's תולדות are like רגל

steps.title: Pebbles: half damage from a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא meant צרורות, pebbles kicked up by an animal's foot, which pay only חצי נזק based on a הלכה passed down by tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He meant the half damage of pebbles, which is a law we know by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב פפא meant צרורות, a תולדה of רגל that pays only half, unlike regular רגל, which pays in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pebbles kicked up by a walking animal fall under רגל, yet they pay only חצי נזק. That makes them a תולדה that is not like its אב. This is not written in the תורה but was passed down as a הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks
half the cost of the damage
we learned it as a law passed down by tradition

steps.whatToRemember: The different תולדה רב פפא meant is צרורות: a תולדה of רגל that pays only חצי נזק because of a tradition.
steps.confusionAlert: צרורות still belong to the category of רגל. They are not a separate category; they are an exception within רגל that pays only half.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that צרורות pay חצי נזק, which comes up many times in the מסכת.

phrases.english: About the half damage of pebbles,
which is a law we learned by tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּחֲצִי נֶזֶק צְרוֹרוֹת, דְּהִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by pointing to a special case within רגל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All of רגל's תולדות are like רגל, so רב פפא could not mean רגל
steps.terutzMaskana: צרורות are a תולדה of רגל with a different law (חצי נזק), so רב פפא was right

steps.title: Why call pebbles a subcategory of foot damage?
steps.stepSummary: If צרורות pay only חצי נזק, unlike רגל, why are they labeled a תולדה of רגל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why does he call it a subcategory of רגל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the last step. If pebbles pay differently from רגל, why group them under רגל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תולדה is supposed to share the law of its אב. רגל pays full damages, but צרורות pay only half. So the label 'תולדה of רגל' seems to have no point.

keyTerms.meaning: A subcategory of רגל (damage done by an animal's foot while walking)

phrases.english: But why does he call it
a subcategory of Foot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20 that רב פפא meant צרורות.
steps.kashyaTarget: Calling צרורות a תולדה of רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A subcategory should share its parent's law, but צרורות pay half while רגל pays full.

steps.title: It shares payment from the best property
steps.stepSummary: צרורות are linked to רגל because the payment comes from the owner's best-quality property.
steps.simpleTranslation: To pay from the best-quality property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that pebbles are like רגל in one way. The owner pays from his best property, not only from the animal itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally חצי נזק, like the חצי נזק of a שור תם, is paid only from the body of the animal that did the damage. צרורות pay half, but like רגל they are paid from the owner's general best property. That shared feature earns the label תולדה of רגל.

phrases.english: To pay from the best-quality property.
phrases.notes: Most חצי נזק, like an ox that gored for the first time, is paid only from that animal's own body. This answer says pebbles are different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a shared legal feature that justifies the label
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the payment amount differs, צרורות have nothing in common with רגל.
steps.terutzMaskana: They share the manner of payment: from the owner's best property, like רגל.

steps.title: But רבא was unsure about this very point
steps.stepSummary: רבא asked whether the חצי נזק of צרורות comes from the animal's body or from the best property, so the answer cannot be taken for granted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא raise this as an open question? For רבא asked: the half-damage of pebbles, does one pay it from the animal's body, or from the best property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. רבא was never sure that צרורות are paid from the best property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer depends on the fact that צרורות are paid from עליה. But רבא left exactly that question unresolved. An open question cannot be the reason for a fixed label.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a question he could not settle
The half-damage owed for pebbles kicked up by an animal
From its body, meaning from the damaging animal itself

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking how much is paid. Everyone agrees it is half. He is asking which assets the half is paid from.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava raise this as a question?
For Rava asked:
the half-damage of pebbles,
does he pay it from its body,
or does he pay from the best-quality property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that צרורות are paid from עליה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא treated the payment source as an open question, so it cannot be the obvious reason for the label.

steps.title: רבא was unsure, but רב פפא was certain
steps.stepSummary: The question belongs to רבא. For רב פפא it was obvious that payment comes from עליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא it is a question. For רב פפא it is obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two different אמוראים held two different positions. רב פפא was sure that צרורות are paid from the best property, so his label makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's doubt does not bind רב פפא. רב פפא took it as a given that payment comes from עליה, and that is why he called צרורות a תולדה of רגל.

phrases.english: For Rava it is a question;
for Rav Pappa it is obvious.
phrases.notes: Obvious that the payment comes from the best-quality property.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָבָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, לְרַב פָּפָּא פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's doubt undermines the reason given for רב פפא's label.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא held it was certain, so for him the reason stands.

steps.title: For רבא, what links pebbles to foot damage?
steps.stepSummary: רבא is unsure about the payment source, so for him what makes צרורות a תולדה of רגל?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבא, who is unsure, why is it called a subcategory of רגל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question again, this time from רבא's side. Without a certain payment source, what does he see in common with רגל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא the shared feature from step 22 is not certain. The גמרא needs a different shared feature to explain the label according to him.

phrases.english: According to Rava, who has it as a question,
why is it called a subcategory of Foot?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרָבָא דְּמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, אַמַּאי קָרֵי לַהּ תּוֹלָדָה דְרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question of step 21, now according to רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תולדה label according to רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The payment-source reason is uncertain for רבא, so the label still needs a justification.

steps.title: Exempt in the public domain, like רגל
steps.stepSummary: צרורות are a תולדה of רגל because, like רגל, they are exempt when the damage happens in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exempt it in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that pebbles share another law with רגל. The owner is exempt if the damage happens in the public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רגל is exempt in רשות הרבים, because animals naturally walk there. Calling צרורות a תולדה of רגל teaches that they get the same exemption. That works even for רבא, who is unsure where the payment comes from.
steps.whatToRemember: צרורות pay only חצי נזק, but they are still a תולדה of רגל. Everyone agrees they are exempt in רשות הרבים. רב פפא also holds they are paid from the best property (עליה), which רבא left as an open question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a תולדה does not have to match its אב in every law. It is enough to share a key feature, here the exemption in the public domain.

phrases.english: To exempt it in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different shared legal feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a certain payment source, צרורות have no link to רגל according to רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: They share the exemption in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: What does the word מבעה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words מבעה and הבער and asks what מבעה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'the מבעה and the הבער, etc.' What is 'מבעה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and asks what the unusual word מבעה refers to. This question sets up the dispute that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the סוגיא dealt with the אבות and their תולדות, looking for the one רב פפא meant. Now the גמרא goes back to the משנה's own wording to identify which damager the word מבעה stands for, because the word itself is not clear.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the four main damagers in the משנה; its meaning is the question here
Fire, the damager listed next to מבעה
'Etc.', short for the rest of the משנה's line

phrases.english: The maveh and the fire, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה at the start of the פרק, which lists שור, בור, מבעה, הבער.

phrases.english: What is "maveh"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of צרורות as a תולדה of רגל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which damager is meant by the word מבעה in the משנה.

steps.title: רב says a person, שמואל says eating
steps.stepSummary: רב explains מבעה as אדם (a person who damages); שמואל explains it as שן (an animal's eating).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: מבעה means a person. שמואל said: מבעה means the tooth, meaning eating.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different answers to the question of what מבעה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real dispute about which damager the משנה counts under this name. For רב, the four damagers include a person. For שמואל, מבעה is the animal's eating, which the משנה would otherwise not mention by name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Tooth', the category of an animal eating and damaging

steps.confusionAlert: שן does not mean only damage done with teeth. It is the name of the category of an animal eating for its own benefit.

phrases.english: Rav says: Maveh, this is man,
and Shmuel says: Maveh, this is the tooth (eating).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מַבְעֶה זֶה אָדָם, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מַבְעֶה זֶה הַשֵּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 with two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: מבעה is a person (אדם). שמואל: מבעה is eating (שן).

steps.title: רב's source: a verse about asking
steps.stepSummary: רב brings a פסוק from ישעיהו where the root בעה means 'to ask,' which only a person does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said מבעה is a person, as it is written: 'The watchman said: morning has come, and also night; if you will ask, ask.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רב gets his reading. He points to a פסוק that uses the same root as מבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the words תבעיון and בעיו mean 'ask' or 'seek.' Asking is something a person does, so רב reads מבעה as a word about a person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you will ask, ask', from the same root as מבעה
'As it is written', introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: Rav says: Maveh, this is man,
as it is written: "The watchman said:
Morning has come, and also night;
if you will inquire, inquire."
phrases.notes: These two words share a root with מבעה. Asking is something only a person does.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר מַבְעֶה זֶה אָדָם, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא itself repeats רב's statement in order to add his source.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that מבעה means a person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 21:12, where the root בעה means asking, a human act.

steps.title: שמואל's source: a verse about hidden things revealed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל brings a פסוק from עובדיה with the word נבעו, from the same root as מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said מבעה is the tooth, as it is written: 'How is עשו searched out, how are his hidden places revealed (נבעו).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows שמואל's source. He points to a different פסוק that also uses the root of מבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is נבעו. At this point it is not yet clear how this word relates to eating, so the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A word from the same root as מבעה, used about עשו's hidden things

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: Maveh, this is the tooth,
as it is written: "How is Esau searched out;
how are his hidden places revealed."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר מַבְעֶה זֶה הַשֵּׁן, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 29: now שמואל's source is given.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that מבעה means שן.

steps.title: How does this verse point to eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word נבעו in שמואל's פסוק shows that מבעה means eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it show?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how שמואל's פסוק connects to eating. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about עשו's hidden things, not about animals eating. So the link between נבעו and שן needs to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does it imply?', asks how a source proves the point

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how שמואל's source actually supports him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word נבעו relates to an animal's eating.

steps.title: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation: 'revealed'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's תרגום renders נבעו as 'were revealed,' which fits teeth that show when an animal eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates: How is עשו searched out, his hidden things were revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of the פסוק. It shows that נבעו means 'revealed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the root means 'to be revealed,' then מבעה refers to something that gets uncovered. An animal's teeth are hidden when its mouth is closed and become revealed when it eats, so מבעה means שן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As he translates', quoting an Aramaic translation of a פסוק

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translates:
How is Esau searched out;
his hidden places are revealed.
phrases.notes: So נבעו means 'revealed', like teeth that show when an animal opens its mouth to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 by giving the meaning of נבעו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נבעו means 'were revealed,' so מבעה refers to teeth that are revealed while eating.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב agree with שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב does not accept שמואל's reading, since it seems well supported.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, what is his reason that he did not say like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that שמואל's proof looks strong, the גמרא challenges רב to explain why he rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב יוסף's תרגום shows that the root can mean 'revealed,' שמואל's reading fits well. So רב needs a reason to reject it.

phrases.english: And Rav, what is the reason
that he did not say as Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמואל's source is explained, the גמרא challenges רב's position.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל has a clear source showing that the root means 'revealed,' so why would רב not accept it?

steps.title: The משנה says מבעה, not נבעה
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה uses the active form מבעה, not the passive form נבעה, which would be the right word for teeth that are revealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: Does the משנה say 'נבעה'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends himself by looking closely at the exact grammar of the word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teeth are revealed, which is passive, so the word for them should be נבעה. The משנה says מבעה, an active form, which fits a person who actively does something. So the grammar supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The passive form, 'that which is revealed'
'Does it teach...?', a rhetorical question pointing to the exact wording of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רב: מבעה is a person (from 'asking'). שמואל: מבעה is שן (from 'revealed,' as in רב יוסף's תרגום). רב rejects שמואל's reading because the משנה uses an active word, not the passive נבעה.

phrases.english: He could have said to you: Is it taught "niveh"?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה would say נבעה, 'is revealed,' if it meant teeth. It says מבעה, an active word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33 on רב's behalf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the grammatical form of the word in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the root can mean 'revealed,' רב should agree that מבעה means שן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's active form מבעה does not fit something that is revealed (נבעה), so רב reads it as a person.

steps.title: Why doesn't שמואל read it like רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around and asks why שמואל does not accept רב's reading that מבעה means אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, why didn't he say like רב?
steps.whatsHappening: In the last steps the גמרא asked why רב rejects שמואל's reading. Now it asks the same question the other way: why doesn't שמואל accept רב's reading?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads מבעה as אדם, a person who does damage. The גמרא wants to know what is wrong with that reading in שמואל's eyes.

phrases.english: And Shmuel, what is the reason
that he did not say like Rav?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 33, now challenging שמואל instead of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's refusal to read מבעה as אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's reading seems reasonable too, so שמואל needs a reason to reject it.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה doesn't say בועה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that if the משנה meant a person doing damage, it would say בועה, not מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: does the משנה say 'בועה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. He points to the exact form of the word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant a person doing the damage himself, the fitting word would be בועה. Since the משנה says מבעה instead, שמואל holds it does not mean אדם. Each side now has a grammar argument against the other.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (this is how he would answer)
Does it teach? (does the משנה say?)
The form of the word for a person who does the damage himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the three forms. In step 34 רב said 'נבעה' would fit revealed teeth. Here שמואל says 'בועה' would fit a person. The משנה actually says 'מבעה'.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Does it teach "bo'eh"?
phrases.notes: He means that 'בועה' would be the word for a person doing damage himself, and the משנה doesn't use it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grammatical precision in the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מבעה could easily mean a person who does damage.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person doing damage would be called בועה, so מבעה does not mean אדם for שמואל.

steps.title: The פסוקים don't decide, so why does רב reject שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that neither side's פסוק fits the exact word, so the argument must rest on something else. It asks again for רב's real reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, the פסוקים don't fit precisely for either one. So why didn't רב say like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: neither פסוק matches the exact form מבעה, so the proofs from פסוקים cancel each other out. That sets up a fresh question about what really drives רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's פסוק (about asking) would fit the form בועה, which is why שמואל objected in step 36 that the משנה does not say בועה. שמואל's פסוק (about being revealed) would fit the form נבעה, which is why רב objected in step 34 that the משנה does not say נבעה. Neither matches מבעה exactly, so the real dispute cannot be about the פסוקים, and the גמרא looks for a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, now that we see

phrases.english: After all, the verses
are not precise according to this Master
and are not precise according to that Master,
phrases.notes: The two 'Masters' are רב and שמואל.

phrases.english: Rav, what is the reason
that he did not say like Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי קְרָאֵי לָא כְּמַר דָּיְיקִי וְלָא כְּמַר דָּיְיקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from פסוקים and opens a new search for רב's reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the פסוקים don't decide, רב's grammar point is not enough by itself, so he needs a deeper reason.

steps.title: רב: 'שור' already covers everything an ox does
steps.stepSummary: רב's reason: the משנה already lists שור, which covers all damage done by an ox, including eating. So מבעה must be something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught 'שור', and that includes everything an ox does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב's real reason. Eating is already covered by the word שור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שור includes every kind of ox damage (horn, tooth, foot), then reading מבעה as eating would just repeat what שור already says. So רב reads מבעה as something new: אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the תנא of the משנה) taught
All matters of an ox, every kind of damage an ox does

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the dispute really rests on how to read the structure of the משנה, not on the פסוקים.

phrases.english: He taught "ox"
and all matters of an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the structure of the משנה to avoid repetition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rejection of שמואל rested only on the wording of the פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since שור covers all ox damage, מבעה must refer to something else: אדם.

steps.title: The same problem for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with רב's own point: the משנה already says שור, so why list eating separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for שמואל too: the משנה already taught 'שור'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses שמואל. If שור already covers everything an ox does, reading מבעה as eating repeats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's argument from the last step now becomes an attack on שמואל. שמואל has to explain why the משנה would list tooth damage separately.

phrases.english: And Shmuel too,
but the Tanna taught "ox" for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל נָמֵי, הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ שׁוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 38 against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of מבעה as eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שור already includes eating, so listing מבעה as eating would repeat it.

steps.title: רב יהודה: שור is the horn, מבעה is the tooth
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains שמואל's view. שור means only the horn and מבעה means the tooth. The משנה lists them separately to show how they differ: the horn gets no pleasure from the damage, but the tooth does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: 'שור' was taught for its horn, and 'מבעה' for its tooth. This is what the משנה means: the horn, which gets no pleasure from its damage, is not like the tooth, which does get pleasure from its damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge for שמואל. He says שור does not cover every kind of ox damage; it means only the horn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, שור means קרן (goring) and מבעה means שן (eating). They are listed separately because they work differently: goring gives the animal no pleasure, while eating does. So מבעה adds a new category and repeats nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means
Pleasure from the damage it does

steps.whatToRemember: For רב, מבעה means אדם because שור covers all ox damage. For שמואל, שור means only קרן and מבעה means שן. They differ because the tooth enjoys its damage and the horn does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל removes the tooth from the category of ox damage. Both are an ox's damage. שמואל only says the word שור in this משנה refers to the horn.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
He taught "ox" for its horn,
and "maveh" for its tooth.
And this is what he is saying:
The feature of the horn is not,
where there is no pleasure in its damage,
like the feature of the tooth,
where there is pleasure in its damage.
